text: You're at the gate, ticket in hand, ready for your flight. All you want is to get to your seat, stash your bag, and relax. Simple, right?
But as boarding begins, the smooth flow you imagined becomes a slow, shuffling queue. You inch forward, then stop. Inch, then stop again.
Why is it always like this? Is it just disorganized people blocking the aisle, fumbling with bags? Your simple model of chaos seems to fit.
The real reason is a complex system: the narrow aisle, overhead bins filling, and boarding groups that don't truly optimize for speed, only processing tickets.
The true cost isn't just wasted time; it's the frustration of inefficient design. Airlines prioritize early access or baggage fees over a faster boarding experience.
Next time you board, you'll see past the shuffling feet. You’ll understand the invisible system governing this dance, and maybe even find a moment of Zen.
